title: Open, closed, both, or neither

prereqs.why: You need the definition — every point has a ball inside the set — rather than a picture of a boundary.
Closed is defined as "the complement is open", which is not the negation of open.

statement:
Work in $\R$ with the usual metric. Select every set below that is **open in $\R$**.

Remember that open and closed are not opposites: a set can be both, and most sets are neither.
hints: A set $U$ is open when for every $x \in U$ there is some $r > 0$ with $B(x,r) \subseteq U$. Apply that literally, point by point, and pay attention to endpoints.
For each set, the question is whether there is a point with *no room around it*. One such point is enough to stop the set being open.
$\R$ itself and $\emptyset$ are both open — and both closed. For the finite set, ask what $B(x,r)$ looks like around one of its points.

payload.prompt: Select every set that is open in $\R$.
